title: Spans and arrays
description: Arrays, spans, and ranges in C#

exercises.title: Create Slice
exercises.description: Create a slice with make for 3 ints. Assign values 1,2,3. Print using Console.WriteLine.
exercises.starter_code:
var s = new int[3];
// assign 1,2,3 and print
hints: Fixed buffers use stack arrays or `new int[length]` assignments.

exercises.title: Append to Slice
exercises.description: Create slice nums = list[1, 2}. Append 3, 4, 5. Print result.
hints: Reach for `List<int>` semantics with `.Add`/`.AddRange` for amortized resizing.
Clone into display layout matching earlier exercises.

exercises.title: Slice Length and Capacity
exercises.description: Create slice s = make([]int, 3, 10). Print its len and cap.
hints: After filling three sentinel entries, `.Count` reports logical length.
`List<T>.Capacity` mirrors the preallocation story from other tracks.

exercises.title: Slice Literals
exercises.description: Create slice fruits = list["apple", "banana", "cherry"}. Print its length.
hints: Array literals behave like contiguous sequences; `.Length` is the quick count.

exercises.title: Slicing a Slice
exercises.description: Create slice n = list[1,2,3,4,5}. Slice it to get [2,3,4] (elements at index 1,2,3). Print result.
hints: LINQ `.Skip`/`.Take` mirror half-open slicing when you dislike manual indices.
Alternatively leverage range syntax `.AsSpan()[start..end]` for zero-extra-allocation slicing.
Remember to import `System.Linq` when chaining LINQ operators.

exercises.title: Append Slices
exercises.description: Create two slices: a = list[1, 2} and b = list[3, 4, 5}. Append all elements of b to a and Console.WriteLine the result.

exercises.title: Copy Slice
exercises.description: Create slice original = list[1, 2, 3}. Make an independent copy and append 4 to the copy. Print both.
exercises.starter_code:
var original = new[] { 1, 2, 3 };
// copy, append 4, print both
hints: `Clone()` (cast back to `int[]`) or `[..collection]` spreads copy payloads.
Keep `original` untouched while mutating only the duplicated buffer.
Prefer `Concat`/`Append`-then-`ToArray()` when LINQ chaining reads clearer.
